question: Which protein complexes recognize centromeric (CEN) DNA in yeast?

supports.quote: Our results favor a H3-Cse4 heterotypic octamer at the budding yeast centromere
In budding yeast, a single right-handed cenH3/H4/H2A/H2B tetramer wraps the ∼80-bp Centromere DNA Element II (CDE II) sequence of each centromere into a 'hemisome'.

initial_executor.limitations: Evidence is restricted to budding yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae); Schizosaccharomyces pombe evidence (e1) mentions centromere-linked genes but does not identify specific protein complexes recognizing CEN DNA. Evidence e4 notes interaction of H3, Cse4, H4, H2A, and H2B with centromeric DNA, supporting the complex composition.

supports.quote: Our results favor a H3-Cse4 heterotypic octamer at the budding yeast centromere
In budding yeast, a single right-handed cenH3/H4/H2A/H2B tetramer wraps the ∼80-bp Centromere DNA Element II (CDE II) sequence of each centromere into a 'hemisome'.
Here, we show that Cse4 octamers remain intact under conditions of low salt and urea that dissociate H3 octamers.

Surprisingly, we observed a strong interaction of H3, as well as Cse4, H4, H2A, and H2B, but not histone chaperone Scm3 (HJURP in human) with the centromeric DNA. H3 localizes to centromeric DNA at all stages of the cell cycle.

same_evidence_Qwen.limitations: Evidence is restricted to budding yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) and Schizosaccharomyces pombe genes; S. pombe genes (LYS1, CYH1, TPS13, RAN1) are centromere-linked but not described as protein complexes recognizing CEN DNA. Scm3 is explicitly noted as not interacting with centromeric DNA. The term 'cenH3' in e6 refers to Cse4 in budding yeast context.
